content:
maria: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need to decide the cutover approach for the dashboard backend split. TL;DR: surface renderer (ui-proxy) vs query-aggregator (q-accum).

kevin: +1 on splitting, but we need clear auth boundaries. do we keep authz in q-accum or push it to ui-proxy?

sam: my take: push auth checks to ui-proxy for fast-deny and short-circuit. q-accum can trust an internal token for per-tenant batching. fewer roundtrips.

maria: that helps latency, but it increases attack surface on ui-proxy. ui teams want a thin renderer. also complicates canary rollouts when both sides must be version-compatible.

julie: tradeoff: auth-in-ui reduces permission fanout in q-accum but duplicates logic across renderers. auth-in-q means q-accum must be RBAC-aware and potentially do SQL-level pushdown auth filters. which is more sustainable?

lena: for long-term, centralizing auth in q-accum seems cleaner for audits and consistent policy enforcement. short-term, we can short-circuit in ui-proxy for common deny cases and replicate policy checks in both places until migration finishes.

kevin: ok plan: start with ui-proxy deny-first + headers asserting caller identity, route to q-accum which validates a signed assertion header. q-accum accepts only signed requests from trusted proxies. this lets q-accum own final enforcement.

maria: that means we need a token-signing service and a key rotation plan. also fine-grained telemetry to detect mismatches. can we use existing service-token flow?

sam: yes, reuse service-issuer with a new scope claim (render:proxy). rotation: short-lived tokens (5m) with mint endpoint. q-accum will cache signer keys for 60s.

julie: other concern: caching. dashboards rely on per-tenant partial caching (prefix + kvcache). if q-accum enforces auth, caching needs to be namespaced by tenant + permission fingerprint. otherwise we leak results.

lena: suggestion: cache key = tenant_id + permission_hash + query_signature. permission_hash = H(sorted(role_ids)). cheap to compute, stable across requests.

maria: nice. also need invalidation: when role bindings change, we need to evict permission_hash entries. ops: emit event on auth change; q-accum subscribes and purges relevant keys.

kevin: how about query cost accounting and SLOs? separating layers means we measure at ui-proxy and q-accum. which layer records token-level cost?

sam: q-accum should be the source of truth for token costs since it executes queries. ui-proxy records ingress latency and render times. billing hooks will read from q-accum telemetry.

maria: rollout plan proposal:
1) deploy q-accum behind a feature flag (read-only) — mirror mode to verify results.
2) enable ui-proxy header signing + short-lived tokens for a subset of tenants (canary 5%).
3) switch traffic for canary tenants to q-accum enforcement path. monitor diffs via golden prompts and rendering checks.
4) incremental expansion and fail-open fallback to legacy aggregator for mismatches.

julie: addendum: need an automatic diff checker that compares aggregated rows/hash sums between legacy and q-accum to detect logical regressions. even row-order differences can be ignored if checksum matches.

lena: ops: add dedicated dashboards for mismatch rate, auth-failure spikes, cache-hit-perms, and p50/p95 of render path. alert on >0.1% mismatch over 10m.

kevin: performance micro-optimizations: use streaming partial renders from q-accum so UI can hydrate incrementally. also adopt a prioritized fetch for visible widgets only.

sam: small nak: streaming complicates auth tracing and per-token metrics but worth it. ensure trace IDs flow across signed headers.

maria: migration tasks assigned:
- kevin: implement header signing + mint endpoint (ETA 2w)
- sam: q-accum auth verifier + permission_hash cache namespacing (ETA 3w)
- julie: diff-checker + observability dashboards (ETA 2w)
- lena: rollout runbook + eviction event hookup (ETA 1w)

deploy-bot: deploy finished: ui-proxy v23 -> staging at 1788889000 :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks. next sync Friday to review canary metrics. react here with :eyes: when you ack tasks.
